title: Letter informing American Transmission Company LLC that the 07/24/2026 filing is deficient and requesting additional information to be filed within 30 days to assist in processing etc. under ER26-3265.

documents.name: ER26-3265-000.docx
documents.text:
FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION
WASHINGTON, DC  20426

OFFICE OF ENERGY MARKET REGULATION

In Reply Refer To:
American Transmission Company LLC
Midcontinent Independent System Operator, Inc.
Docket No. ER26-3265-000

Issued:  September 22, 2026

American Transmission Company LLC
W234 N2000 Ridgeview Pkwy. Ct.
Waukesha, WI  53188-1022 

Midcontinent Independent System Operator, Inc.
1700 Centerview Drive
Little Rock, AR  72211

Attention:	Stephanie Neitzel, Senior Counsel 
Kalen Coleman

Reference:  Deficiency Letter

Dear Ms. Neitzel and Mr. Coleman:

On July 24, 2026, Midcontinent Independent System Operator, Inc. (MISO), on behalf of American Transmission Company LLC (ATC), submitted four amended and executed Large Load Project Commitment Agreements (LLPCA) and an executed Minimum Transmission Charge Agreement (MTCA) between ATC and Wisconsin Electric Power Company (WEPCo).  ATC states that WEPCo and ATC are currently developing a transmission-distribution interconnection project (T-D Project) to allow WEPCo to serve a data center campus being developed by the Microsoft Corporation (Microsoft) in Racine County, Wisconsin.  ATC explains that the T-D Project involves multiple phases of modifications and expansions to ATC’s transmission system, with some facilities already in service and additional facilities yet to be developed.  

ATC states that the LLPCAs are being amended to provide certain updates to the project scope and costs and to add provisions for the collection of Construction Work in Progress (CWIP) costs (CWIP Charge).  ATC states that under the MTCA, WEPCo is committing to pay 100% of the network integration transmission service rate for transmission capacity it requests from ATC to serve the Microsoft data center campus – either through Schedule 9-ATC of the MISO Open Access Transmission, Energy and Operating Reserve Markets Tariff (Tariff) or through a minimum transmission charge.  ATC asserts that the LLPCAs and MTCA work jointly to prevent the unjust shifting of transmission costs.  ATC requests a July 1, 2026 effective date for the LLPCAs and MTCA.  

Please be advised that your submittal is deficient and that additional information is necessary to process the filings.  Please provide the information requested below.

The introductory paragraph of each LLPCA states, in part, that the LLPCA is “effective upon receipt of all required regulatory approvals contemplated by Section 3.9 hereof.”  Section 3.9 (Disputes) of each LLPCA does not address regulatory approvals.

Please explain the discrepancy in the reference to section 3.9.

Please explain whether there are any pending regulatory approvals, or if any regulatory approval was granted after July 1, 2026.  If so, please explain how this reconciles with ATC’s requested July 1, 2026 effective date in the instant filing and whether this would impact the collection of the CWIP Charge.

Section 3.3 (Obligation to Reimburse Project Costs) of each LLPCA states that upon termination, cancellation, or substantial change, WEPCo shall reimburse to ATC all expenditures, costs, and cancellation fees incurred, or due to commitments made by ATC (collectively, Project Costs) to construct the facilities described in Exhibit A to each LLPCA (LLPCA Project).  In addition, section 3.3 of each LLPCA describes the obligation of WEPCo to reimburse ATC for Project Costs, stating in part, “[i]n the event of termination of this [LLPCA] due to the completion of the [LLPCA Project], and the [LLPCA Project] being put into ATC’s rate base (as described in Section 3.10(a)), the reimbursement obligation set forth in this Section 3.3 shall not apply.”  The LLPCAs do not contain section 3.10(a).

Please indicate the applicable section in the LLPCA that describes the LLPCA Project being put into ATC’s rate base such that the reimbursement obligation set forth in section 3.3 shall not apply. 

Section 5.1 (Survival) of each LLPCA states that, “[WEPCo]’s obligations under Sections 3.3, 3.4 and 3.6 shall survive any termination or cancellation of this Agreement.”  The amended LLPCAs include a new section 3.5 (Amounts to Be Directly Charged), and as a result, sections 3.6 (Mitigation) and 3.7 (Payment of Reimbursable Project Costs) have been renumbered. 

Please confirm whether section 5.1 of each LLPCA intends to refer to section 3.6 or if it should be revised to refer to section 3.7.

Section 3.4 (Amounts to be Reimbursed) of each LLPCA states that upon termination, cancellation, or substantial change of the LLPCA, WEPCo will reimburse ATC for the Project Costs, including any applicable tax gross-up charges.  In the event the LLPCA Project is terminated, cancelled, or substantially changed:

Please provide ATC’s proposed accounting for its receipt of WEPCo’s reimbursement for the incurred Project Costs, including the gross-up for the current tax liability that ATC would be responsible to remit to the Internal Revenue Service.  In addition, please confirm that ATC will separately record the portion of the cash receipt related to the tax gross-up from the portion related to the cancelled LLPCA Project.  

Please explain how the tax gross-up charges are calculated.  In addition, please clarify whether the tax gross-up charges will be determined based on the tax rates reflected in ATC’s formula rate in Attachment O of MISO’s Tariff.

Section 9(B)(c)(i)(2) of the MTCA states, “If during the term of the MTCA the aggregate, cumulative amount of Minimum Transmission Charge and the Customer Load Project Schedule 9 Charge paid by [WEPCo] reaches the Minimum Transmission Charge Liability Cap, [WEPCo] will no longer pay the Minimum Transmission Charge” (emphasis added).

Please confirm whether WEPCo will pay the customer load project Schedule 9 charge under this MTCA and, if so, please explain whether this charge is duplicative of the monthly payments WEPCo makes under Schedule 9-ATC of MISO’s Tariff given that section 9(B) of the MTCA states, “For clarity, separate from this MTCA, [WEPCo] remains responsible for paying the Network Integration Transmission Service Charge pursuant to Schedule 9-ATC of the MISO Tariff.”  

If WEPCo will not pay the customer load project Schedule 9 charge under this MTCA, please confirm whether the minimum transmission charge liability cap applies to the aggregate, cumulative amount of minimum transmission charges paid by WEPCo under the MTCA and the amount ATC recovers from WEPCo for the T-D Project under Schedule 9-ATC of MISO’s Tariff.  

Section 9(B)(c)(i)(3) of the MTCA states, “The Minimum Transmission Charge Liability Cap applies to any Early Termination Fee incurred pursuant to this MTCA.”  Section 14(F)(b) (Early Termination Fee) states, “The Early Termination Fee will equal the aggregate monthly Requested Transmission Capacity multiplied by the Network Rate in effect at the time of the termination event for the remainder of the Term of this MTCA.”

Please confirm, if WEPCo pays ATC an early termination fee, whether the minimum transmission charge liability cap applies to the aggregate, cumulative amount of minimum transmission charges, the customer load project Schedule 9 charge, and the early termination fee.

Alternatively, if WEPCo does not pay the customer load project Schedule 9 charge under this MTCA, please confirm, if WEPCo pays ATC an early termination fee, whether the minimum transmission charge liability cap applies to the aggregate, cumulative amount of minimum transmission charges, the amount ATC recovers from WEPCo for the T-D Project under Schedule 9-ATC of MISO’s Tariff, and the early termination fee.

Section 13 (Term) of the MTCA states that unless terminated earlier, the term of the MTCA shall commence on the effective date and continue until the later of 15 years after the in-service date of the final tranche of transmission capacity, as defined by the requested transmission capacity schedule, or upon “payment of all outstanding payment obligations of [WEPCo] to ATC under this MTCA.”

Please explain why 15 years after the in-service date of the final tranche of transmission capacity was selected as the term for the MTCA and why such a term for the MTCA is just and reasonable.

Exhibit C (Security Schedule) to the MTCA provides the security schedule that sets forth the security amount WEPCo is responsible for providing during the term of the MTCA, subject to the minimum transmission charge liability cap.

Please provide cost support that shows that the Schedule 9 rate used in the security schedule is the current network rate at the time of execution, as stated in Exhibit C to the MTCA.

Please provide additional cost support that explains how the estimated annual network charge, and the estimated remaining network charges in the security schedule, are calculated.  

Exhibit F (Minimum Transmission Charge Liability Cap Schedule) to the MTCA provides the minimum transmission charge liability cap equal to the aggregate incremental revenue requirement for the T-D Project over its useful life.  Exhibit F to the MTCA states that the minimum transmission charge liability cap is calculated using ATC’s formula rate in Attachment O of MISO’s Tariff.

Please provide additional cost support that explains how the minimum transmission charge liability cap is calculated, using ATC’s formula rate in Attachment O of MISO’s Tariff.  

Please provide the necessary formulas and cost support for and clarify the estimated initial capital cost for each LLPCA Project, the period over which each LLPCA Project is depreciated, the book depreciation rate and tax depreciation rate used for each LLPCA Project, the post-tax weighted average cost of debt and equity used from ATC’s capital structure, and any other cost support necessary to demonstrate how the minimum transmission charge liability cap was calculated.  

Please explain how the useful life of the T-D Project is determined.

This letter is issued pursuant to 18 C.F.R. § 375.307 (2025) and is interlocutory.  This letter is not subject to rehearing pursuant to 18 C.F.R. § 385.713 (2025).  A response to this letter must be filed with the Secretary of the Commission within 30 days of the date of this letter by making a deficiency filing in accordance with the Commission’s electronic tariff requirements.  To the extent that some of the requested information may include privileged information or other confidential information, please submit a non-public version in addition to a public version for Commission review, in accordance with 18 C.F.R. § 388.112 (2025).  For your response, please use Type of Filing Code 180, Deficiency Filing.  The information requested in this letter will constitute an amendment to your filing, and a new filing date will be established.  A notice will be issued upon receipt of your filing.

Failure to respond to this letter within the time period specified may result in a
further order rejecting your filing.

Issued by:  Natalie Y. Tingle-Stewart, Director, Division of Electric Power Regulation – Central
